memory_update.text: OII is the best US-listed underfollowed candidate for this node so far: public Navy evidence links it to Virginia-class support equipment, submarine rescue systems, subsea/seabed warfare, and Freedom AUV development, while market labeling often remains offshore-energy/subsea services.

CODA should remain in the funnel as a below-USD-300M speculative exception because it is one of the few US-listed micro-caps with explicit proprietary subsea imaging sonar and defense engineering exposure.
MIND is a weaker speculative-shadow candidate: relevant sonar/maritime-security/ASW language exists, but current materiality to defense or submarine programs must be proven before advancing.

US-listed mappings for naval/submarine niche components are often hidden in mixed industrial labels: offshore energy services, marine technology, sonar/seismic equipment, aerospace-defense technologies, and defense engineering services.
Later layers should explicitly test whether candidate exposure is program-critical and qualified/sole-source, or merely adjacent project work with limited chokepoint power.

node: Naval, submarine, and subsea niche components
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe for naval, submarine, and subsea niche components. The strongest direct US-listed mapping is not the obvious European micro-supplier lead but a mixed set of US-listed naval hardware, subsea robotics, sonar/imaging, and marine-security equipment names. Reference lane: Curtiss-Wright anchors the established submarine-content mapping. Underfollowed lane: Oceaneering, Coda Octopus, and MIND Technology appear closer to second-order subsea, underwater imaging, maritime-security, support-equipment, or autonomous-undersea chokepoints, but two are micro-cap speculative exceptions below the preferred USD 300M threshold and require later filing-level validation.
